title: add-jsonschema-strict-mode-improved-error-reporting-openai-compat
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: Close gaps in JSON Schema structured output handling when using the OpenAI compatibility layer. Users reported silent schema validation failures and opaque errors when response_format=json_schema with strict=true. This PR adds a strict-mode validation path that returns deterministic, OpenAI-compatible error objects, improves server-side preflight validation, and ensures streaming responses that violate schema are terminated cleanly with structured error metadata.

What this changes (high level):
- Add strict-mode validation pipeline for response_format=json_schema that runs both fast preflight checks and final schema validation after generation.
- Emit OpenAI-compatible error payloads when the model output cannot be coerced to the schema in strict mode (error types, message, and suggestion fields).
- Improve streaming stability: when a mid-stream validation failure is detected we now close the stream with a structured error event instead of silent truncation.
- Add opt-in compatibility flag openai_compat.strict_schema_errors (defaults to false) to preserve current behavior unless explicitly enabled.
- Update SDK error mapping in redwood-openai-compat to surface the new structured errors as exceptions with error.code and error.suggestions.
- Add e2e tests and unit tests for both preflight and post-generation validation, including sampled model outputs and edge cases (arrays, oneOf/anyOf, additionalProperties).

Checklist:
- [x] Core validation pipeline implemented
- [x] OpenAI-compatible error schema defined and documented
- [x] Streaming path updated to send structured error events and terminate cleanly
- [x] Unit + e2e tests added and passing locally
- [x] Docs and migration notes added to the API reference

Migration notes:
- Behavior is opt-in via openai_compat.strict_schema_errors=true. Customers who rely on permissive coercion should not see any change until they enable the flag.
- Breaking-change risk: low when flag is disabled; enabled mode can cause previously-tolerated outputs to be rejected. See release_notes for recommended rollout steps.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-2045 (schema validation refactor), PM-312 (product acceptance criteria), SUP-789 (customer report about opaque errors).

release_notes:
Add opt-in strict JSON Schema response_format (openai_compat.strict_schema_errors). When enabled, responses that cannot be validated against the provided schema will return a structured OpenAI-compatible error object and terminate streaming with a structured error event. Recommended rollout: enable in staging, exercise representative prompts, then enable for customers with explicit acceptance.

Migration: opt-in flag set to false by default. No immediate breaking changes unless enabled.
